newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Louisiana sweet crudes gain on thin imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Louisiana sweet crudes gain on thin imports.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes remained slightly weaker Wednesday afternoon, while Louisiana sweet grades advanced as a result of higher-priced Brent offerings.
Traders said differentials for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James improved to 24 cents over the West Texas Intermediate/Cushing benchmark, nearly 10 cts higher than the weakest deals spotted on Tuesday.
Brent barrels were heard on offer for the March 10-15 window at March WTI minus 12 cts, moving higher on a narrowing arbitrage window between the corresponding Brent/WTI, traders said.
LLS was left to gain as a result of the more expensive Brent, and talk only two players were "seriously offering."
Currently, March WTI was ranging around the $24.00 a barrel level, nearly even with the Tuesday close.
Other trades were heard for West Texas Sour at a $2.30 discount to the WTI/Cushing, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 32 cts over and Eugene Island at minus $2.48.

Midland/WTI remained weak, talked at a 37-40 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing. Talk that a major buyer of Midland had stored February barrels, and was currently selling both February and March barrels has kept the market weak.

Outside news was scarce today, with no major influence seen from the neutral to slightly bullish inventory data released by the American Petroleum Institute (API) on Tuesday and the U.S. government this morning.
